The Index of Consumer Sentiment is one of three indexes derived from the University of Michigan’s Surveys of Consumers, which started in 1946. Originally conducted annually, the surveys switched to a monthly cadence in 1978. The surveys have a sample size of roughly 600 people selected randomly from the 48 adjoining U.S. states and the District of Columbia. [...] The Index of Consumer Sentiment registered at 51.0, down from 55.2 in July.
 Current Economic Conditions registered at 51.8, down from 54.8 in July.
 The Index of Consumer Expectations registered at 50.6 down from 54.4 in July.
